model: BVPS compounding x exit P/B (residual-income-style insurer model, cost of equity discount)

inputs.shares_outstanding_basis: cover-page shares outstanding, 10-Q filed 2026-07-31, as of 2026-07-31 (most current diluted proxy; weighted-average diluted shares for Q2-2026 were 533.6M, cover-page count reflects the buyback pace since then)
inputs.net_debt_note: Insurer model: no net-debt deduction. AIG's ~$9.2bn of holding-company debt funds investable float backing policy liabilities, not operating leverage on a cash-flow stream; it is already inside the book-value base being compounded. Deducting it again would double-count exactly the trap the routing skill (owner-fcf-adaptations 'never subtract net debt from an already-post-financing flow') warns against for a bank/insurer.
inputs.goodwill_note: ~$3.4bn goodwill vs $40.6bn equity (~8%); tangible book ~$71.9/share vs $77.66/share book. Not separately modeled -- the gap is small and stable, so book and tangible book compound at effectively the same rate here. Flagged for a future update if a segment impairment moves it.
inputs.sbc_source: not applicable -- insurer model; SBC/FCF adjustments belong to the owner-FCF engine, not this route
inputs.buyback_cash_note: H1-2026 cash buybacks $1,153m (Q1 $508m + Q2 $645m); FY2025 was $5,836m -- pace has moderated as the Corebridge/Validus divestiture proceeds have been substantially redeployed, consistent with a normalizing (not runway-driven) repurchase program going forward
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T16:05:43Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 71.25-87.29
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% base-case cost of equity for a large-cap global P&C insurer: US risk-free ~4.2%, ERP ~5.5%, beta modestly above 1 given catastrophe/reserve-development volatility and the ongoing CEO transition. Bull case -0.5pp (post-Corebridge simplification reduces complexity discount); bear case +1.0pp (reserve-adequacy and cat-loss tail risk repriced). All in USD, matching the USD-denominated equity base -- no currency adjustment needed.
inputs.nci_treatment: not applicable -- no material NCI post-Corebridge/Validus full divestiture
inputs.notes: AIG is now (post May-2026 full exit of Corebridge Financial and the 2023 Validus Re sale) a pure-play global commercial + personal P&C insurer -- Analysis JSON confirms three segments (North America Commercial, International Commercial, Global Personal), no more spread-based life/annuity income. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book -> BVPS compounding x exit P/B', not owner-FCF: reported operating/free cash flow for an insurer reflects investment-portfolio and float timing, not a distributable owner-FCF stream, and 'net debt' is investment leverage backing policy reserves, not operating debt to subtract. This is a fresh build (no prior Drivers.json or DCF.json existed for AIG). The engine (make build-dcf) is NOT used for this model -- per SKILL.md and the dcf-analyst contract, the non-FCF routes fill the same JSON fields by hand. Historical BVPS (period-end equity / period-end shares) shows genuine per-share compounding despite ~$6bn/yr of capital return: $77.5 (FY19) -> $59.19 (FY22, Corebridge IPO deconsolidation + AOCI mark-to-market on rising rates) -> $72.13 (FY25) -> $77.66 (Q2-26), because the share count fell from 870m (FY19) to 523m (current), a ~40% reduction, more than offsetting the equity base shrinkage from divestiture proceeds paid out. Core operating ROE was 11.1% in Q2-2026 (11.6% H1-2026) against management's own 10-13% through-FY2027 target (2024 Investor Day, reaffirmed Q2-2026) -- the base case ROE path ramps toward the low-to-mid end of that band rather than assuming the guided range is hit immediately.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: bvps_3yr_cagr (FY2022 $59.19 -> FY2025 $72.13, period-end equity / period-end shares; the further step to the current $77.66 Q2-2026 anchor reflects five more months of the same compounding, not a change in trend). Total shareholders' equity CAGR is negative and misleading here because it mixes the Corebridge/Validus divestiture payouts (real cash returned to shareholders, not value destruction) with organic book growth -- BVPS is the metric that isolates per-share compounding net of buybacks.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Total-equity CAGR (-1.8% 3yr, -9.3% 5yr) diverges sharply and mechanically from BVPS CAGR (+6.8% 3yr, -1.6% 5yr) because ~$20bn+ of equity left the balance sheet via Corebridge/Validus divestiture proceeds paid out as buybacks/dividends over 2021-2025, shrinking the total equity base while the share count fell far faster in percentage terms (870m FY19 -> 523m current, ~40%), so BVPS still compounded. Equity CAGR is not a usable growth signal for this ticker; BVPS CAGR is used instead, per the routing skill's book-value/ROE approach for insurers. The 5yr BVPS CAGR is still slightly negative because FY2020 (pre-divestiture, $77.99) predates the Corebridge separation; the 3yr window (post-separation-in-progress, FY2022 on) is the cleaner read of the current pure-play P&C compounding rate and is what selected_growth_rate uses.

base.narrative: Core operating ROE continues its post-turnaround recovery, ramping from ~9.5% (2026, still short of the 10-13% Investor Day band) to 11.5% by year 5 -- the middle of management's target range, not the top. Payout ratio (dividends only; buybacks are captured implicitly through per-share BVPS compounding on a shrinking share base, so are not double-counted as a separate cash outflow) rises modestly from 22% to 30% as the extraordinary post-divestiture buyback pace normalizes. Exit multiple 1.05x book reflects AIG trading near-book historically (rarely sustaining a premium given its reserve-development history) with modest credit for the post-Corebridge simplification story.

bull.narrative: Management hits the top of its 10-13% core operating ROE target by 2027 and holds it -- expense ratio sustainably below 30%, Global Personal combined ratio near 94%, no adverse reserve surprises, and new CEO Andersen's broker relationships (ex-Aon) drive incremental profitable growth. The market re-rates AIG toward a Chubb-/Travelers-like multiple (1.3x book) as the simplified, pure-play underwriting story is rewarded and the complexity discount closes. Cost of equity 50bp lower reflecting reduced business-mix complexity post-divestiture.

bear.narrative: Softening commercial property/specialty pricing cycle (flagged in Analysis JSON as already underway) compresses underwriting margins faster than expense-ratio discipline can offset; AIG's decades-long history of adverse reserve development on long-tail casualty resurfaces with a charge, and the CEO transition (external, first-time carrier CEO) disrupts underwriting culture continuity. ROE settles near 8%, below the low end of the guided range. Market applies a discount-to-book multiple (0.85x), close to where AIG traded through much of 2016-2020 during its prior underperformance era. Cost of equity +100bp for the reserve/execution risk repricing.

scenario_narratives.base: Core operating ROE ramps from ~9.5% to 11.5% over 5 years (middle of the 10-13% Investor Day band), book value per share compounds via retained earnings on a shrinking share count, exit at 1.05x book, discounted at 9.5% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: ROE reaches the top of guidance (13%) and holds; multiple re-rates to 1.3x book on the post-divestiture simplification story; 9.0% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: Softening pricing cycle plus a reserve charge and CEO-transition execution risk hold ROE near 8%, below guidance; multiple falls to 0.85x book (near AIG's pre-turnaround trading range); 10.5% cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25 rather than a tighter bear weight. AIG carries genuine tail risk the 25% bear case is meant to capture: a first-time external carrier CEO, a multi-decade history of adverse reserve development on long-tail casualty that has resurfaced repeatedly across cycles, and a commercial property/specialty pricing cycle that is turning from hard to soft. None of these is a solvency risk (balance sheet is de-risked post-divestiture, no material near-term refinancing need), but they are real enough to earnings quality that a 15% bear weight would understate the range of outcomes.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: House and street bases coincide for this model (no SBC/GAAP-vs-adjusted-FCF distinction applies to a book-value compounding model); band_position is not meaningful here and is reported null rather than a misleading 0.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AIG is valued as a book-value compounder: the relevant question is not a projected free cash flow stream (reported operating cash flow reflects investment-portfolio and reserve timing, not a distributable owner-FCF measure) but how fast book value per share grows through retained core operating earnings and a shrinking share count, and what multiple of that book value the market will pay at exit. The base case has AIG compounding BVPS from $77.66 to ~$114 over five years (average ~8%/yr) while returning a growing but still-modest dividend, exiting at roughly today's ~1x book multiple. At $74.13 the stock trades at a slight discount to today's $77.66 book value already, which provides some margin of safety independent of the ROE-improvement thesis playing out.
key_risks_to_valuation: Adverse reserve development on long-tail casualty lines -- AIG's most persistent historical risk, capable of taking a multi-billion-dollar charge directly against book value with no warning
CEO transition execution risk: Eric Andersen is an external hire and first-time insurance-carrier CEO succeeding the architect of the underwriting turnaround
Softening commercial property/specialty pricing cycle could compress margins faster than the expense-ratio and mix-improvement offsets management is targeting
Catastrophe losses (wildfire, hurricane, severe convective storm) create quarter-to-quarter earnings and book-value volatility independent of the underlying trend
Buyback pace naturally moderates now that Corebridge/Validus divestiture proceeds are substantially redeployed, removing a mechanical BVPS-per-share tailwind of the last several years
Rate-cutting cycle would gradually compress net investment income on the float, a real earnings headwind the ROE path does not explicitly break out
